title: Which Receipt Is Missing?
observable_outcome: The learner identifies a missing receipt from a checklist, asks which receipt is missing, and confirms the submission deadline.
learning_objective: Ask which expense receipt is missing, identify the claim date and amount, and confirm the submission deadline.

scenario.prompt: Your 18 September expense claim totals €76: train €42, lunch €18, and taxi €16. The checklist shows the train and lunch receipts are attached. The taxi receipt is missing. Finance says: Please upload it by 4 p.m. Wednesday.
scenario.puzzle: Which receipt is missing, which claim is it from, how much is it, and when must you upload it?
scenario.privacy_note: The workplace, claim, receipts, amounts, colleague, and deadline are fictional teaching data. This activity is language practice, not accounting, tax, legal, or financial advice.

model.clarify: Which receipt is missing from my 18 September expense claim?
model.colleague_reply: The taxi receipt for €16 is missing.
model.confirm: So I need to upload the €16 taxi receipt by 4 p.m. Wednesday, right?
model.neutral_variant: Which receipt do I need to upload for my 18 September claim?

language_focus.grammar: In Which receipt is missing?, which receipt is the subject, so there is no do-support. In Which receipt do I need to upload?, which receipt is the object, so present-simple question order uses do + subject + base verb.
language_focus.meaning: Missing means not attached to the claim. The claim date identifies the form; the category and amount identify the receipt. By 4 p.m. Wednesday means no later than that time, not only at exactly 4 p.m.
language_focus.appropriateness: Ask a neutral question, name the claim date, then read back the category, amount, and deadline. This checks details without blaming the colleague.
language_focus.detail_language: Expense processes and evidence rules vary by employer and location. Follow the actual policy and ask the responsible team when unsure.

choice_activity.prompt: Which receipt is missing from the 18 September claim?

options.feedback: Correct. The checklist marks train and lunch as attached, leaving the taxi receipt missing.
The train receipt is attached. Look for the category without a check mark.
The lunch receipt is attached. The missing category is taxi.

request_activity.prompt: Which question is grammatically well formed and useful here?

options.text: Which receipt is missing from my 18 September claim?
options.feedback: Correct. Which receipt is the subject of is missing, so no do is needed.

options.text: Which receipt does missing from my 18 September claim?
options.feedback: Do not use does before missing in this subject question. Say Which receipt is missing?

options.text: Why did you lose my receipt?
options.feedback: This assumes blame and does not identify the missing item. Ask which receipt is missing first.

slot_activity.prompt: Match each detail to its job in the readback.

feedback.claim date: Correct. This identifies the expense claim.

feedback.receipt category: Correct. This names the missing receipt type.

feedback.amount: Correct. This distinguishes the taxi expense by value.

feedback.deadline: Correct. By means no later than this time.

production_task.scenario: A 6 October claim lists parking €12 and lunch €21. The parking receipt is attached, but the lunch receipt is missing. Finance asks for it by noon Friday.
production_task.instruction: Write one neutral question that identifies the claim. Then write a readback with the missing category, amount, and deadline.
acceptable_responses: Which receipt is missing from my 6 October claim? So I need to upload the €21 lunch receipt by noon Friday, right?
Which receipt do I need to upload for the 6 October claim? The €21 lunch receipt is due by noon Friday, right?
rubric: I asked which receipt was missing without assigning blame.
I included the category and amount.
I confirmed the deadline with by.
production_task.valid_variants: Which receipt is missing? and Which receipt do I need to upload? are both valid, but their grammar differs because the question phrase has a different job. Can you confirm ...? is also acceptable.

review_prompt: Tomorrow, recall the four readback slots: claim date, receipt category, amount, and deadline. Make one question and one confirmation.

design.reference_limit: The reference title/page was verified earlier. Full playback and frames were not inspected. No artwork, characters, music, footage, or software dependency was copied.
design.texture: Restrained fibres and speckles generated procedurally.
design.depth: Folders, receipt cards, labels, people, upload tray, and clock use cream cut edges, overlap, and offset shadows.
design.motion_principle: The claim folder opens; receipt cards fan out; check marks attach while the taxi gap reveals; a question card unfolds; the taxi receipt slides into an upload tray while the deadline clock rises; a new claim repeats the evidence pattern. Captions remain fixed.
design.accessibility: Dark navy text on cream panels; every colour-coded date, category, amount, and deadline also has a word label and distinct shape.

visual.title: Claim, category, amount, deadline
visual.alt_text: A colourful layered papercut evidence path. An 18 September expense claim shows train €42 and lunch €18 attached, while taxi €16 is missing. Arrows lead to ask which receipt is missing and confirm upload by 4 p.m. Wednesday.
visual.prose: First identify the claim by date. Scan the receipt checklist and find the category without a check mark. Read its amount. Ask which receipt is missing, then confirm the category, amount, and deadline.
